newsitem.title: JAPAN: Qatar minister says OPEC quota should be kept.
newsitem.headline: Qatar minister says OPEC quota should be kept.

text.p: Qatar's Energy and Industry Minister Abdullah bin Hamad al-Attiyah said on Thursday OPEC's quotas should not be raised to strike a supply and demand balance after Iraq comes back to the international oil market.
"I believe they (quotas) should not be raised. Iraq is coming to the market and to achieve a balance between demand and supply, quotas should be rolled over," he said.
The minister said talks between three Japanese trading houses and Qatar regarding taking a partial stake in the second LNG project in the country will be concluded by the end of October.

He said that a portion of the project will be sold to the Japanese trading houses, which are Sumitomo Corp, Itochu Corp, and Nissho Iwai. Qatar General Petroleum Corp has a 70 percent stake in the project and Mobil Corp has the remaining stake.
At the last OPEC meeting in June, there were suggestions the quotas could be raised at the next meeting in November.
OPEC quotas were kept steady at the June meeting except for an additional 800,000 barrels-per-day for Iraq's expected return to the market.

Energy and Industry Minister Abdullah bin Hamad al-Attiyah is in Japan for a ceremony marking the first liquefied natural gas (LNG) vessel to carry Qatari term gas cargoes to Japan. He will be here until Saturday.
Sumitomo Corp, Nissho Iwai Corp and Itochu Corp have been seeking to acquire a combined 10 percent stake in the second project Ras Laffan LNG Co (Rasgas), traders said.
The minister declined to say how large the stake would be.
The Rasgas project is expected to start production in 1999.
